# MCP tool reference

The 26 tools the server offers, read from a running server.

The core server installs and manages the others, and looks after this machine. Start it with `agentcomms mcp`,
or register it with a client with `agentcomms mcp install --client claude-code` — from a terminal, since it is
the one registration that cannot come from chat. Every tool runs the operation its `agentcomms` command runs.

**Every change is shown to a person first.** A changing tool’s first call returns `approvalRequired`, a
`preview` and an `approvalId`; the same tool called again with the same arguments and that id applies it —
after the person’s yes in the conversation under the `chat` change policy, or after they run
the approve command the result gives, at their own terminal, under `confirm` — `comms_approval_wait` says when
they have, and `comms_approval_revoke` withdraws one they said no to. No tool approves a change, and none
applies a change it did not plan itself.

### `comms_paths`

Where the configuration, state, data, secrets and downloads live on this machine.

*read-only*

Takes no arguments.

### `comms_doctor`

Check this machine: Node, the directories, the configuration, account names, the standing approvals in force and when each ends, the secret store, managed CLI shims, and which MCP clients start each server — each check with the fix when it fails. `ok` is false when any check fails; a check with `warn` is something to look at, and leaves `ok` true.

*read-only*

Takes no arguments.

### `comms_audit_tail`

The most recent audit records, newest last: every send, change and approval step, with the surface it came from. Filter by mailbox and time.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inbox` | string | no | only this mailbox, as `organisation/gmail` |
| `since` | string | no | only records at or after this ISO time |
| `limit` | integer | no | at most this many; 50 when left out |

### `comms_activity`

What this agent session — the window that started this server — read, was told, did and sent through agent-communications: its own calls only, never another session's. Each line: when, the channel and account, the operation, its kind (read, write, told, approval), its outcome (ok, refused, failed) and why, how long it took, and what it touched — ids, and subjects, senders and file names inside the untrusted-content envelope; never a message body. Newest first, with the session's counts: the latest 50 lines of the last 24 hours by default — `limit` returns up to 200, and `since` looks further back; `more` says when more matched. Filter by kind, channel, account, outcome and time. A window whose grouping could not be read — always on Windows, and in a folder such as `/` or the home folder that cannot tell projects apart — shows nothing here: its calls are still recorded, each process on its own. Reads only.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `read` \\| `write` \\| `told` \\| `approval` | no | only calls of this kind |
| `channel` | string | no | only this channel: `gmail`, `slack`, `resend`, `whatsapp`, `events` |
| `account` | string | no | only this account, by its name — `organisation/platform` — or its id |
| `outcome` | `ok` \\| `refused` \\| `failed` | no | only calls that ended so |
| `since` | string | no | only calls at or after this: an ISO time, or a span back from now such as `7d` or `12h`; the last 24 hours when left out |
| `limit` | integer | no | the most lines to return, newest first: 50 when left out, 200 at most |

### `comms_approval_revoke`

Cancel an approval so it can never be used: a send, a post, or a configuration change the person said no to. Refusing is never the dangerous direction, so this asks nobody.

*writes · idempotent*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `approvalId` | string | **yes** | the approval to revoke |

### `comms_approval_wait`

Wait for an approval — a send, a post, a change or a download’s question — to be usable or finished, and say where it stands: pending (with `claimable` true when a yes in the chat can use it), approved, being sent, used, failed, unknown, expired, revoked, corrupt, or answered for a question. A standing approval's wait ends `active` once the person has approved it — it is used through its channel's acknowledgement, never claimed — and `standing` says pending, active or ended, with why. `waitSeconds` is 30 when left out, 300 at most, and 0 for its status now. It only looks: it never approves, claims or sends. Ended still waiting, wait again — never prepare it again while it is pending or being sent.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `approvalId` | string | **yes** | the approval to wait for |
| `waitSeconds` | integer | no | how long to wait: 30 when left out, 300 at most, 0 for the status now |

### `comms_channels_available`

Which channel servers exist (core, Gmail, Resend, Slack, WhatsApp), which are on this machine and at which version, and which MCP clients start each — with the version an entry pins and whether a file it starts has gone. Reads files only.

*read-only*

Takes no arguments.

### `comms_change_policy`

Report or set the change policy — how a loosening is approved: `chat`, a yes in this conversation, or `confirm`, a code the person types at their own terminal — for the defaults, one mailbox, or one account or workspace. Without `set` it only reports. Tightening to `confirm` applies at once. Loosening to `chat` is itself a change, approved under the policy in force, `confirm`: the person runs the approve command the result gives, at their own terminal, before you call again with the id. A mailbox or account or workspace that sets `chat` itself keeps it when the default is tightened: the result then carries `warning` and `looser`, each with the call that tightens it — show the warning to the person.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inbox` | string | no | one mailbox, as `organisation/gmail` |
| `account` | string | no | one account or workspace, as `organisation/resend`, `organisation/slack` or `organisation/whatsapp` |
| `set` | `chat` \\| `confirm` | no | the policy to set; leave out to report |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_attach`

Report or change which local files may be attached to a draft, an email or a post: the folders they may come from, the paths they never may, and the built-in list the jail always applies. With no change it only reports. Otherwise exactly one of `rootsAdd`, `rootsRemove`, `denyAdd`, `denyRemove`, a path absolute or starting with `~`. Allowing another folder, or removing a deny entry, is a change the person approves: the first call returns the preview — which says where a link leads — and an approvalId; call again with it once they agree. Removing a folder, or adding a deny entry, narrows what can be attached and applies at once. The built-in list cannot be changed.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rootsAdd` | string | no | let files under this folder be attached — approved first |
| `rootsRemove` | string | no | stop attaching files from under this folder — at once |
| `denyAdd` | string | no | never attach files from this path — at once |
| `denyRemove` | string | no | take this path off your own deny entries, so files there can be attached again — approved first |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_activity_settings`

Report or change whether this machine records what agent sessions read, were told, did and sent — the activity log, private to this machine: ids, subjects, senders, searches and recipients, never a message body — and for how many days. With no change it only reports. Otherwise exactly one of `record` or `retentionDays`. Turning recording off, or keeping fewer days, applies at once, and fewer days deletes the older ones at once. Turning it back on, or keeping more days, is a change the person approves: the first call returns the preview and an approvalId; call again with it once they agree. Change it only when the person asked.

*writes · destructive*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `record` | `on` \\| `off` | no | `off` stops recording at once; `on` records again — approved first |
| `retentionDays` | integer | no | how many days the log keeps, 1 to 365: fewer applies at once, more is approved first |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_label`

Report or change how what an agent sends is labelled: the person's name and a word in parentheses — "Jo Example (agent)" — so recipients can tell the agent sent it. With no change it only reports: the word, the name, every rule, and for each account and kind of message whether it goes out labelled or as the person. Otherwise exactly one of `word`, `name`, `addRule`, `removeRule`, `icon`, `style`. A new word, name or icon, a rule `as: "me"`, removing an `agent` rule, and a Slack workspace's `style` set to `labelled` are changes the person approves: the first call returns the preview — the phrase recipients will see, or what each kind of message will now be — and an approvalId; call again with it once they agree. A rule `as: "agent"`, removing a `me` rule, or a style back to `app`, applies at once. Add a `me` rule, or choose `labelled`, only when the person asked for that.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word` | string | no | the word after the name: one of agent, assistant, twin, minion, bot, fake, AI, written exactly so |
| `name` | string,null | no | the name, for where a channel has no name of its own for the person; null clears it |
| `addRule` | object | no | who a kind of message appears to come from, on one account |
| `removeRule` | object | no | a rule to take away, as it is listed |
| `icon` | object | no | the icon of the agent’s Slack posts in one workspace |
| `style` | object | no | how an agent’s messages look in one Slack workspace |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_behaviour`

Report or change which acts an agent may start at all — post, reply, reaction, edit, delete, file, send — on each account and in each conversation; every act it may start still waits for the person's yes to its exact content. With no change it only reports: every rule, and for each account what is allowed across it and in each conversation a rule names. Otherwise exactly one of `setRule` — only these acts there, replacing the rule at that level; `acts: []` allows nothing — or `removeRule`. A change that only narrows what is allowed applies at once. One that allows more anywhere — an act added, a rule removed whose fallback is wider, a conversation allowed more than its account — is a change the person approves: the first call returns the preview, each level before → after, and an approvalId; call again with it once they agree. Start one that allows more only when the person asked for it.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setRule` | object | no | what an agent may do in one place: the rule for it, added or replaced |
| `removeRule` | object | no | a rule to take away, by its account and conversation, so the wider one holds there |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_standing`

Report, narrow or end the standing approvals: acknowledgements — a standard emoji reaction, or a short fixed reply the person wrote — that an agent may send without asking, on a message that has just arrived from another person, within the places, counts and days the person set. With no change it only reports: each one's state, its contents, each named by its digest, its places and limits as in force, when it ends, its uses in the last day and its last 10 acts. Otherwise exactly one of `narrow` — keep fewer contents or places, lower a limit, or end it sooner — `revoke`, which ends one, or `off`, which ends every one. Each applies at once and asks nobody, since each only takes away; one that would allow more is refused. Nothing here creates or widens one: that is prepared on Slack and approved by the person at their own terminal, with its code. End one, or all, whenever the person asks.

*writes · destructive · idempotent*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `narrow` | object | no | what to keep of one standing approval: it applies at once |
| `revoke` | object | no | end one standing approval at once, and every act of it not yet sent |
| `off` | boolean | no | true ends every standing approval at once |

### `comms_profile`

How the person wants a message written in one place — tone, language, length, sign-off, threads — from the Markdown files they keep: their own instructions to you, not content from anyone else. Call it before writing a message, for the account it goes from and the conversations it goes to, and follow it; where it and what the person asks in this conversation disagree, what they ask wins. For mail pass each recipient’s address and then its `@domain`, in recipient order; for a Slack DM its `D…` id and then the person’s `U…` id; for a channel its `C…` id. Returns the joined text, each part marked with the file it came from, and every file it would read, written or not. It only reads, and needs no approval. No tool writes a profile: the person starts a missing file at their own terminal, with the core CLI’s `profile init`.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | string | no | the account the message goes from: `acme/slack`, `acme/gmail`; left out, only the layers every message shares |
| `conversations` | string[] | no | the conversations it goes to, in order: for mail each address then its `@domain`; for a Slack DM the `D…` then the `U…`; for a channel its `C…` |

### `comms_orgs_list`

The organisation profiles added here: each one’s label, where it was read from and its SHA-256, its Google clients (which is active, which mailboxes use each) and its Slack apps, and any drift with the call that repairs it. Never includes a client secret or the profile’s contents.

*read-only*

Takes no arguments.

### `comms_org_show`

One organisation profile: its label, source and SHA-256, its Google clients and their mailboxes, its Slack apps, any drift from what was approved, each with the call that repairs it, and `extensions`: which of the profile’s extensions are applied here, and which are not, with the release each needs. Never includes a client secret or the profile’s contents.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `organisation` | string | **yes** | the organisation, as the first half of its account names: `rgc` |

### `comms_org_add`

Add an organisation’s profile — the small JSON file naming its Google OAuth client and Slack apps — so its members’ accounts can use them, beside whatever is here already. Pass the file’s path on this machine; never ask for its contents in the conversation, and never read it yourself. A change: the first call returns the preview — the organisation, the file and its SHA-256, the Google client and the name it gets or the client it uses, the Slack workspace and apps — and an approvalId; call again with it once the person agrees. If the file changes in between, the claim is refused and the change is prepared again. The client secret is never shown or returned.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | **yes** | where the profile file is on this machine, e.g. ~/src/rgc-agentcomms/rgc.agentcomms.json |
| `forOtherAddresses` | boolean | no | also let this organisation’s client serve the person’s mailboxes outside it — only when they ask |
| `adopt` | string | no | the OAuth client already registered here to use as the organisation’s, when its client id is registered under more than one name |
| `store` | `keychain` \\| `file` | no | where secrets are kept, only when this writes the first one here: keychain (default) or file |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_org_update`

Read an organisation profile again from its file, apply what changed in it, and repair drift — a client of the organisation’s that was removed or changed here. A changed profile, a new `source`, and `forOtherAddresses: "on"` are a change: the first call returns the preview listing each change before → after ("secret changed" for a new client secret) and an approvalId; call again with it once the person agrees. Repairing drift, a tighter update cap from the organisation, and `forOtherAddresses: "off"` apply at once, even beside a change that waits, and are listed in the result; a looser cap is approved first. An extension the profile marks optional that this release does not know is skipped and named in `extensions`; one it marks required refuses the update (NEEDS_NEWER_RELEASE), changing nothing — update first, then call it again.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `organisation` | string | **yes** | the organisation, as the first half of its account names: `rgc` |
| `source` | string | no | read the profile from this file from now on |
| `forOtherAddresses` | `on` \\| `off` | no | `on` lets its client serve the person’s other mailboxes too (approved first); `off` applies at once |
| `adopt` | string | no | the OAuth client already registered here to use as the organisation’s, when its client id is registered under more than one name |
| `store` | `keychain` \\| `file` | no | where secrets are kept, only when this writes the first one here: keychain (default) or file |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_org_remove`

Forget an organisation profile, and delete the OAuth clients it made here with their secrets; clients the person registered themselves are left as they are. Refused while a mailbox signs in through one of its clients, or a client still marked as its own no longer matches it — the refusal says what to run first. A change that cannot be taken back: the first call returns the preview naming every client it removes and an approvalId.

*writes · destructive*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `organisation` | string | **yes** | the organisation, as the first half of its account names: `rgc` |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_server_install`

Register a channel’s MCP server — `gmail`, `resend`, `slack`, `whatsapp`, or `core` (this one) — with an MCP client, and prove it starts. A change: the first call returns the preview and an approvalId; call again with it once the person agrees. `print` only returns the entry to paste, and asks nobody. An install that registers nothing — the client’s own command cannot be found — or whose server does not start is an error, with the entry to paste in its `details`. The new server appears after the client is restarted — tell the person.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | `core` \\| `gmail` \\| `resend` \\| `slack` \\| `whatsapp` \\| `events` | **yes** | which server |
| `client` | `claude-code` \\| `claude-desktop` \\| `codex` \\| `cursor` \\| `gemini` \\| `vscode` \\| `json` | **yes** | which MCP client to register it with |
| `name` | string | no | the name the client shows; the channel’s own when left out. 1–64 of A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ - |
| `account` | string | no | a channel server that declares accounts: serve this one, named `organisation/<channel>` — the same as `inbox` for Gmail and `workspace` for Slack |
| `inbox` | string | no | Gmail only: serve this one mailbox |
| `workspace` | string | no | Slack only: serve this one workspace |
| `readOnly` | boolean | no | Gmail only: leave out every tool that changes a mailbox |
| `launcher` | `managed` \\| `npx` \\| `local` | no | `managed` (default) installs this exact version once; `npx` fetches it on every start |
| `force` | boolean | no | replace this server’s own earlier entry of the same name — how an upgrade reaches a client |
| `print` | boolean | no | only return the entry to paste; write nothing |
| `noVerify` | boolean | no | do not start the server to check the entry works |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_server_prune`

Remove the managed runtimes that no client config names, no printed entry names, no process runs and no stable launcher starts or keeps for a rollback — what upgrades leave behind. One newer than this release, or than what its stable launcher starts, stays: an update may be installing it. With no `channel`, every managed server’s, listed by server; with one, only that server’s. `dryRun` only lists them, and asks nobody. Removing them is a change: the first call returns the preview and an approvalId. While an update is under way on this machine, removing is refused and nothing changes: try again in a few minutes.

*writes · destructive*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | `core` \\| `gmail` \\| `resend` \\| `slack` \\| `whatsapp` \\| `events` | no | whose runtimes; left out, every managed server’s |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | only say what would be removed |
| `includePrinted` | boolean | no | also remove runtimes kept only because an entry for them was printed, once those entries are gone |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_server_uninstall`

Take one server — `channel` — out of one MCP client’s configuration: every entry of it there, at user scope, whatever it is called, and nothing else. A tightening: it applies at once and asks nobody, and takes no approvalId. A project’s own entry is left, and the result says where it is; what was removed is saved first, to put back by hand. The client keeps the server it started until it is restarted — tell the person. Not `comms_server_prune`, which removes unused runtimes and no registration.

*writes · destructive*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | `core` \\| `gmail` \\| `resend` \\| `slack` \\| `whatsapp` \\| `events` | **yes** | which server to take out |
| `client` | `claude-code` \\| `claude-desktop` \\| `codex` \\| `cursor` \\| `gemini` \\| `vscode` | **yes** | which MCP client to take it out of |

### `comms_update`

Bring this machine to the latest published release. `check: true` reads the npm registry and this machine and returns what is behind — `{ latest, behind, upToDate, unpinned, moves, unreadable }`, `moves` being the registrations the next update moves onto the stable launcher — asking nobody. `status: true` reads only this machine's files and returns where updates stand — `{ level, set, by, cap, pausedUntil, lastChecked, latest, running, security, lastError, job }`, `job` being the background job's `{ state, where, installedAt, lastRun, working }` — asking npm nothing. Without either, a change: the first call returns a preview listing every step and an approvalId — each client registration of core, Gmail, Resend, Slack or WhatsApp registered again at the latest version with exactly its name, client, scope, launcher and pins; each managed runtime that needs installing; each global @agentcomms package updated — and the call again with the approvalId, once the person agrees, applies it and reports each step. A registration that starts a stable launcher is not registered again: its launcher is switched to the new release, and no client configuration is edited. Nothing behind: it says so and prepares nothing. The new servers load only after each client is restarted: tell the person, then prune the old runtimes with comms_server_prune. `rollback: true` switches every stable launcher back to the release before, also a change the person approves.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check` | boolean | no | only report what is behind and what is up to date; change nothing |
| `status` | boolean | no | only say where updates stand here — the level and what decided it, any pause, the last check, the latest and running versions, a security fix waiting, and the background job — read from local files, asking npm nothing |
| `noVerify` | boolean | no | do not start each registered server to check that it answers |
| `level` | `auto` \\| `every-14-days` \\| `never` | no | how this machine updates: `auto` checks daily (and installs in the background once that is set up), `every-14-days` at most once every 14 days, `never` asks npm nothing. A level that updates less is a change the person approves: the first call returns its preview and an approvalId; one that updates more applies at once |
| `pause` | any | no | hold every update notice on this machine for 1, 7 or 14 days — `true`, or 7, when the person names no length. A plain answer: no approval. A security fix is never held |
| `resume` | boolean | no | end a pause at once |
| `backgroundJob` | `on` \\| `off` | no | set up or remove the per-user job that installs verified releases in the background, once a day. `on` is a change the person approves: its preview names the job file and what it runs, when it runs, what macOS shows and how to remove it. `off` applies at once |
| `rollback` | boolean | no | switch every stable launcher back to the release it started before its last switch, editing no client configuration. A change the person approves: the first call returns its preview and an approvalId |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_names_migrate`

Rename every mailbox and workspace to `organisation/platform`. `dryRun` shows the mapping and changes nothing. Applying it is a change — the old names stop working — so the first call returns the preview and an approvalId; pass the same `renames` again with it.

*writes · destructive*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `renames` | string[] | no | overrides, each `old=new`; qualify a name both maps use as `inbox:old=new` or `account:old=new` |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | only show the mapping |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |

### `comms_secrets_migrate`

Move every credential between the system keychain and files on this disk, and delete the originals. A change: out of the keychain loosens how they are kept, and the originals cannot be brought back — so the first call returns the preview and an approvalId. Never returns a credential.

*writes · destructive*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | `keychain` \\| `file` | **yes** | where credentials should be kept |
| `approvalId` | string | no | leave out the first time. The approval this tool returned, once the person has agreed to its preview — in the chat under `chat`, with the approve command the result gives under `confirm` |
